([[Spanish Lake, Missouri]]) | college = [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] (2020–2025) | highlights = * Second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[U.S. Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] ([[2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2025]]) * Third-team All-American – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[Sporting News|SN]] (2025) * [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award]] (2025) * [[Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award|Naismith Defensive Player of the Year]] (2025) * [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] (2025) * 4× [[Big East Conference|Big East]] Defensive Player of the Year (2022–2025) * 2× First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2023, 2025) * Second-team All-Big East (2024) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|the {{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Ryan Thomas Kalkbrenner''' (born January 17, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]]. He is from [[Florissant, Missouri]]. ==High school career== Kalkbrenner played basketball for [[Trinity Catholic High School (St. Louis)|Trinity Catholic High School]] in [[St. Louis|St. Louis, Missouri]].{{cite web |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Big East, beware: Creighton's Ryan Kalkbrenner is coming to block your shots |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/plus/big-east-beware-creightons-ryan-kalkbrenner-is-coming-to-block-your-shots/article_49bb247f-6c49-5366-b0c4-1d1433d3ad18.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=June 7, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 13.9 points, 7.6 rebounds and 3.9 blocks per game, earning AAA Player of the Year and Class 3 All-State honors.{{cite web |last1=Woodcock |first1=Rees |title=Illinois Basketball: Illini offer 2020 big man Ryan Kalkbrenner |url=https://writingillini.com/2019/03/28/illinois-basketball-illini-offer-2020-big-man-ryan-kalkbrenner/ |website=Writing Illini |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=March 28, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Beasley |first1=Joe |title=Rim Protecting Big Man named to MOsports Super 50 |url=https://mosports.rivals.com/news/rim-protecting-big-man-named-to-mosports-super-50 |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=February 11, 2020}} Kalkbrenner competed for Mac Irvin Fire on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit, and was named [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] Defensive Player of the Year in 2019.{{cite web |last1=Snow |first1=Brian |title=Top 75 center Ryan Kalkbrenner heads to Creighton |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Creighton-Bluejays-basketball-top-75-Ryan-Kalkbrenner-commitment-136002556/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=September 23, 2019}} In his senior season, Kalkbrenner averaged 16.3 points, 11 rebounds and 5.7 blocks per game, repeating as a Class 3 All-State selection.{{cite web |title=C: Ryan Kalkbrenner, senior, Trinity |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/all-metro/boys-basketball/c-ryan-kalkbrenner-senior-trinity/article_5243d32a-6aed-11ea-8fca-8f596bdddb36.html |website=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=March 28, 2020}} A consensus four-star recruit, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] over offers from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Recruiting: 2020 center Ryan Kalkbrenner commits to Creighton |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/recruiting-2020-center-ryan-kalkbrenner-commits-to-creighton/article_0d6d5981-10bf-51cc-a8b5-714208c77c3e.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=September 23, 2019}} ==College career== Kalkbrenner came off the bench in his freshman season at Creighton. On December 17, 2020, he recorded a season-high 15 points and five rebounds in a 94–76 win over [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]].{{cite web |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Creighton's reserves, who will be instrumental this year, aim to find consistency |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creightons-reserves-who-will-be-instrumental-this-year-aim-to-find-consistency/article_007c2d78-4803-11eb-ba19-8b8db1ca1c7d.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=December 27, 2020}} As a freshman, Kalkbrenner averaged 5.9 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game, leading all [[Big East Conference|Big East]] freshmen in blocks.{{cite web |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Creighton's Ryan Kalkbrenner honored to represent US at U19 World Cup |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creightons-ryan-kalkbrenner-honored-to-represent-us-at-u19-world-cup/article_3aca13e0-d963-11eb-a01a-0bd83704a35e.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=June 30, 2021}} On February 12, 2022, he scored a career-high 22 points and had 15 rebounds in an 80–66 win against [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{cite news |title=Hawkins scores 30 to carry Creighton over Georgetown 80-66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373586 |access-date=February 13, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 12, 2022}} Kalkbrenner was named Honorable Mention All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] as well as Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite news |last1=Schinzel |first1=Gene |title=Ryan Hawkins, Ryan Kalkbrenner and Creighton freshman trio net Big East honors |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/ryan-hawkins-ryan-kalkbrenner-and-creighton-freshman-trio-net-big-east-honors/article_fc691e40-9d7d-11ec-9952-8bce804e7c18.html |access-date=March 6, 2022 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 6, 2022}}{{cite news |last1=Schinzel |first1=Gene |title=Creighton's Ryan Kalkbrenner named Big East Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creightons-ryan-kalkbrenner-named-big-east-defensive-player-of-the-year/article_101e284e-9e33-11ec-a3ed-9bf04670b91c.html |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 7, 2022}} He suffered a knee injury in a 72–69 overtime win over [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] in the NCAA Tournament, ending his season. Kalkbrenner averaged 13.1 points and 7.7 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=NCAA Tournament: Creighton's Ryan Kalkbrenner to miss rest of tourney because of knee injury |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4181177/2022/03/18/ncaa-tournament-creightons-ryan-kalkbrenner-to-miss-rest-of-tourney-because-of-knee-injury/ |access-date=March 18, 2022 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=March 18, 2022}} During the following [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Kalkbrenner scored a career-high 31 points during a 72–63 first round win over [[NC State]].[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401522152 Kalkbrenner leads Creighton past NC State in March Madness] On October 23, 2024, he was named 2024-2025 [[Big East Conference]] Preseason Player of the Year.{{cite web |title=Creighton’s Kalkbrenner Named Preseason Player of the Year |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2024/10/23/mens-basketball-creightons-kalkbrenner-named-preseason-player-of-the-year.aspx |website=www.bigeast.com |access-date=25 October 2024 |language=en |date=23 October 2024}} On November 6, he scored a career-high 49 points in a win over the [[UT Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros men's basketball|UT Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros]] and set a Bluejays record with 20 made field goals.{{cite web |last1=Olson |first1=Eric |title=Ryan Kalkbrenner begins his 5th season at Creighton by scoring a career-high 49 points |url=https://apnews.com/article/creighton-ryan-kalkbrenner-ap-top-25-52e60ab2574197d67dff85762a7306e3 |website=AP News |access-date=November 11, 2024 |date=November 7, 2024}} ==National team career== Kalkbrenner represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged 5.9 points, four rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Rob |title=Kalkbrenner Helps USA Win FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup |url=https://gocreighton.com/news/2021/7/11/mens-basketball-usa-france.aspx |website=Creighton University Athletics |access-date=July 12, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}} == Personal life == Ryan's parents are Kraig and Lynn Kalkbrenner, his brother is Nate Kalkbrenner.{{Cite web |title=Ryan Kalkbrenner - 2024-25 - Men's Basketball |url=https://gocreighton.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ryan-kalkbrenner/8362 |access-date=2025-03-19 |website=Creighton University Athletics |language=en}} He married Rachael Saunders, a Creighton
